checks.why: a == b runs the left operand's __eq__: a test comparing two keys covers what __eq__ calls
a | b runs __or__: composing two strategies covers what __or__ calls
x in c runs the RIGHT operand's __contains__
if x: runs __bool__, and assert x on a class with no __bool__ runs __len__
truth testing falls back to __len__ when the class defines no __bool__
not x truth-tests x through its own __bool__
CONTROL: a class that defines __bool__ is never truth-tested through its __len__
CONTROL: `None or Fallback()` returns the right operand untested, and `is not` runs no dunder
